Therefore, there are plenty of investors who like to buy shares in companies that are growing EPS. Jindal Worldwide managed to grow EPS by 10% per year, over three years. That's a pretty good rate, if the company can sustain it.

Careful consideration of revenue growth and earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) margins can help inform a view on the sustainability of the recent profit growth. It was a year of stability for Jindal Worldwide as both revenue and EBIT margins remained have been flat over the past year. data.title: SLP Resources Berhad's (KLSE:SLP) Earnings Offer More Than Meets The Eye
data.description:
SLP Resources Berhad (KLSE:SLP) announced a healthy earnings result recently, and the market rewarded it with a strong uplift in the stock price. This reaction by the market reaction is understandable when looking at headline profits and we have found some further encouraging factors.

A Closer Look At SLP Resources Berhad's Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

SLP Resources Berhad has an accrual ratio of -0.13 for the year to September 2026. That indicates that its free cash flow was a fair bit more than its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of RM26m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of RM15.6m. SLP Resources Berhad's free cash flow improved over the last year, which is generally good to see.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On SLP Resources Berhad's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, SLP Resources Berhad has perfectly satisfactory free cash flow relative to profit. Because of this, we think SLP Resources Berhad's earnings potential is at least as good as it seems, and maybe even better! And on top of that, its earnings per share have grown at 36% per year over the last three years. data.title: We're Keeping An Eye On Hang Pin Living Technology's (HKG:1682) Cash Burn Rate
data.description:
There's no doubt that money can be made by owning shares of unprofitable businesses. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

So should Hang Pin Living Technology (HKG:1682) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. Let's start with an examination of the business' cash, relative to its cash burn.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Does Hang Pin Living Technology Have A Long Cash Runway?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. In September 2026, Hang Pin Living Technology had HK$91m in cash, and was debt-free. Importantly, its cash burn was HK$43m over the trailing twelve months. So it had a cash runway of about 2.1 years from September 2026. Arguably, that's a prudent and sensible length of runway to have. We should note, however, that if we extrapolate recent trends in its cash burn, then its cash runway would get a lot longer. Depicted below, you can see how its cash holdings have changed over time.

View our latest analysis for Hang Pin Living Technology

How Well Is Hang Pin Living Technology Growing?

Hang Pin Living Technology boosted investment sharply in the last year, with cash burn ramping by 97%. While that's concerning on it's own, the fact that operating revenue was actually down 5.1% over the same period makes us positively tremulous. Taken together, we think these growth metrics are a little worrying. In reality, this article only makes a short study of the company's growth data. You can take a look at how Hang Pin Living Technology has developed its business over time by checking this visualization of its revenue and earnings history.

How Easily Can Hang Pin Living Technology Raise Cash?

Even though it seems like Hang Pin Living Technology is developing its business nicely, we still like to consider how easily it could raise more money to accelerate growth. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. By comparing a company's annual cash burn to its total market capitalisation, we can estimate roughly how many shares it would have to issue in order to run the company for another year (at the same burn rate).

Since it has a market capitalisation of HK$217m, Hang Pin Living Technology's HK$43m in cash burn equates to about 20% of its market value. Given that situation, it's fair to say the company wouldn't have much trouble raising more cash for growth, but shareholders would be somewhat diluted.

Is Hang Pin Living Technology's Cash Burn A Worry?

On this analysis of Hang Pin Living Technology's cash burn, we think its cash runway was reassuring, while its increasing cash burn has us a bit worried. We don't think its cash burn is particularly problematic, but after considering the range of factors in this article, we do think shareholders should be monitoring how it changes over time. The most relevant recent development is the confidential settlement with Marvell that resolves the active electrical cable patent fight and closes US Patent and Trademark Office challenges. That agreement helps protect Credo Technology Group Holding’s ZeroFlap pricing structure and supports its IP based revenue streams across active electrical cables used in AI networking.

For shareholders, this mainly shifts focus back to operational catalysts that Womble highlights, such as sustaining strong gross margins, growing non GAAP net income, and broadening the customer base beyond a few large buyers. Execution risks around new areas like silicon photonics, and any signs of weaker order intake or lower guidance, now matter more than residual legal noise.

Womble’s narrative reaches its US$215.01 fair value for Credo Technology Group Holding by applying projected revenue growth of 20.7% a year and a future profit margin of 49.0%, then pairing those economics with an assumed future P/E in the 55 to 60 times range.

Exploring Other Perspectives

Some of the most optimistic analysts focus less on patent risk and more on whether Credo Technology Group Holding can really hit the ambitious earnings path they were sketching out. Before this settlement, the most bullish group were modelling revenue climbing toward about US$6.1b and earnings of roughly US$2.6b by 2029. That is a very different story to Womble’s high risk fair value view, and this new IP truce could easily nudge those forecasts, in either direction, once analysts refresh their models. Cloudflare (NET) is back in focus after third quarter results showed 39% year over year revenue growth to US$782.5 million, record customer additions, and raised guidance that helped lift the share price.

That earnings beat dropped into a backdrop where Cloudflare’s share price has climbed 54.9% year to date and its 1 year total shareholder return of 58.7% sits on top of a very large 3 year total shareholder return. As a result, the recent 4.1% 1 month share price gain and 0.9% move on the day of the release look more like momentum being reaffirmed than a fresh rerating, even after a 4.7% 7 day share price pullback as investors weigh stronger growth signals against still mixed profitability.

Cloudflare now combines rapid top line expansion with a share price that already reflects a powerful story. Does it make more sense to add exposure at this level, or to wait for a softer entry before running the numbers?

Most Popular Narrative: 81% Overvalued

Cloudflare closed at $303.68, while the leading community narrative pegs fair value closer to $167.45. The story hinges on whether investors are paying far ahead of fundamentals.

According to DaneDruss, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, Cloudflare is less about quantum computing itself and more about securing the transition toward that world.

If Q-Day risk is moving closer, the migration layer may matter as much as the companies trying to build quantum computers. Cloudflare sits closer to the trust-chain side, internet security, network protection, identity, traffic, certificates, and enterprise infrastructure.

See why 30 investors see Cloudflare as 81% overvalued.

DaneDruss anchors the fair value estimate at about $200 per share, using 30% annual revenue growth over five years, a 25% future net margin, a 45x future earnings multiple, a 10% required return, and roughly 375 million diluted shares. That framework treats Cloudflare as a fast growing infrastructure provider where security and post quantum cryptography support customer trust but are not modeled as a big standalone profit pool.

The key tension in that view is simple. The business itself, with US$2,732.8m in revenue and 23% forecast annual top line growth, screens as high quality in terms of potential. Yet the stock already carries a large premium to that narrative fair value and to the SWS DCF estimate of $169 based on future cash flows. For that gap to close on fundamentals rather than price, the narrative argues for either growth holding above 30% for longer, cleaner margin expansion from the current loss of $239.05m, or stronger enterprise pull from post quantum security than is currently built into the model.

Still, Cloudflare’s story could shift quickly if quantum security demand accelerates faster than expected, or if profitability improves sharply against current loss levels.

data.title: Is Now The Time To Put Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure (NSE:TINNARUBR) On Your Watchlist?
data.description:
For beginners, it can seem like a good idea (and an exciting prospect) to buy a company that tells a good story to investors, even if it currently lacks a track record of revenue and profit. Sometimes these stories can cloud the minds of investors, leading them to invest with their emotions rather than on the merit of good company fundamentals. A loss-making company is yet to prove itself with profit, and eventually the inflow of external capital may dry up.

So if this idea of high risk and high reward doesn't suit, you might be more interested in profitable, growing companies, like Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure (NSE:TINNARUBR). Now this is not to say that the company presents the best investment opportunity around, but profitability is a key component to success in business.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

How Quickly Is Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Increasing Earnings Per Share?

Generally, companies experiencing growth in earnings per share (EPS) should see similar trends in share price. So it makes sense that experienced investors pay close attention to company EPS when undertaking investment research. It certainly is nice to see that Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure has managed to grow EPS by 35% per year over three years. If the company can sustain that sort of growth, we'd expect shareholders to come away satisfied.

Top-line growth is a great indicator that growth is sustainable, and combined with a high earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) margin, it's a great way for a company to maintain a competitive advantage in the market. The music to the ears of Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure shareholders is that EBIT margins have grown from 13% to 16% in the last 12 months and revenues are on an upwards trend as well. That's great to see, on both counts.

The chart below shows how the company's bottom and top lines have progressed over time. For finer detail, click on the image.

View our latest analysis for Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure

Since Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure is no giant, with a market capitalisation of ₹18b, you should definitely check its cash and debt before getting too excited about its prospects.

Are Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

Seeing insiders owning a large portion of the shares on issue is often a good sign. Their incentives will be aligned with the investors and there's less of a probability in a sudden sell-off that would impact the share price. So as you can imagine, the fact that Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure insiders own a significant number of shares certainly is appealing. Indeed, with a collective holding of 69%, company insiders are in control and have plenty of capital behind the venture. This should be seen as a good thing, as it means insiders have a personal interest in delivering the best outcomes for shareholders. In terms of absolute value, insiders have ₹12b invested in the business, at the current share price. That should be more than enough to keep them focussed on creating shareholder value!

Is Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Worth Keeping An Eye On?

If you believe that share price follows earnings per share you should definitely be delving further into Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure's strong EPS growth. With EPS growth rates like that, it's hardly surprising to see company higher-ups place confidence in the company through continuing to hold a significant investment. On the balance of its merits, solid EPS growth and company insiders who are aligned with the shareholders would indicate a business that is worthy of further research. We should say that we've discovered 2 warning signs for Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure that you should be aware of before investing here.

Although Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure certainly looks good, it may appeal to more investors if insiders were buying up shares.
